official.deadline_central_display: 1 April 2027 (Master's application and waiver webform, same date); outcomes by 1 June 2027
official.deadline_note: Both the Master's programme application and the Tilburg University Waiver webform must be completed by 1 April 2027 for the September 2027 intake. Waivers are not available for the February intake.
official.status_note: Open for the 2027-2028 academic year; 21 waivers divided by School (TiSEM 6, Law 6, Humanities and Digital Sciences 6, Social and Behavioral Sciences 2, Catholic Theology 1).
official.tuition_coverage_note: 50% waiver of the institutional tuition fee for all regular (non-Research) one-year Master's programmes; the two-year MSc Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence (including its tracks) is also eligible.
official.funding_amount_note: Published as a 50% tuition-fee waiver, not a fixed cash amount; the value depends on the programme's institutional fee.
benefits: 50% reduction of the institutional tuition fee for all regular one-year Master's programmes
Eligibility extended to the two-year Master in Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence, including the AI for Psychological Research and AI en Cybersecurity tracks
eligibility: Completed, or due to complete before the Master's programme starts, the most recent degree in one of the listed eligible countries
This must be the first Master's programme at Tilburg University
Directly admitted to a regular one-year Master's programme (Pre-Master's and Research Master's applicants are not eligible)
Not hold any other tuition-fee waiver
requirements: Submit a complete application for a regular one-year Master's programme starting September 2027 by 1 April 2027
Complete the Tilburg University Waiver application webform before 1 April 2027
documents: Complete Master's programme application submitted by the same deadline
selection_criteria: If more eligible candidates apply than waivers available, selection is by random lottery
Only applicants conditionally or unconditionally admitted to a Master's programme enter the draw
The waiver becomes effective only after unconditional admission is confirmed
coverage: 50% of the institutional tuition fee only
Recipients must still show funds for the remaining 50% of tuition and IND living-cost proof
application_method: Apply for the Master's programme through the standard admission route
Complete the Tilburg University Waiver application form by the same 1 April 2027 deadline
official.application_route: Master's programme application plus separate Tilburg University Waiver webform, both by 1 April 2027
official.citizenship_residency: Non-EEA nationality holders whose most recent degree was completed in one of the listed eligible countries
official.international_eligibility: Open to non-EEA international applicants from the listed eligible countries only
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Regular (non-Research) one-year Master's programmes at Tilburg University
official.duration: One-year Master's programme; the two-year Cognitive Science and AI Master's is also eligible
official.description: The Tilburg University Waiver halves the institutional tuition fee for exceptional international master's applicants who hold a non-EEA nationality and completed their previous degree in an eligible country, with 21 awards each year.

not_confirmed: english_requirement (not published on the scholarship page; programme-level requirements apply)
verification.notes: All facts read live from Tilburg University's own DEI-waiver page on 2026-10-11.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a lottery, not a merit competition: once 21 eligible non-EEA applicants with an eligible-country degree are admitted, selection is random, so the decisive work is meeting the two 1 April 2027 deadlines rather than polishing essays. Plan the unfunded half of the tuition now, because the IND still requires proof of full tuition and living costs before a visa can be lodged.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EEA applicants from the 58 listed countries starting a regular one-year Master's at Tilburg in September 2027 who can fund the remaining 50% themselves.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality is non-EEA and your most recent degree was completed in one of the listed eligible countries
Check that your chosen Master's is a regular one-year programme, not a Research Master's or Pre-Master's
Submit the Master's programme application well before 1 April 2027 so admission is in place for the draw
Complete the separate Tilburg University Waiver webform by the same 1 April 2027 deadline
Budget for the remaining 50% of tuition plus living costs for the IND financial proof
common_rejection_risks: Applying for a Research Master's or Pre-Master's programme, which are excluded
Missing the 1 April 2027 webform deadline even when the programme application is in on time
Holding another tuition-fee waiver, which makes this waiver uncombinable
Assuming the award survives deferral or withdrawal - it is cancelled in both cases
Being counted on for full funding: the IND requires funds for the other half of tuition regardless
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining 50% of the institutional tuition fee, plus housing, food, insurance, books and the IND immigration fee.
document_audit: The waiver form is a short webform, not a dossier - the Master's application carries the academic evidence
Eligibility is judged on nationality and the country of the most recent degree, not on grades
Reserve waivers are only allocated to applicants holding conditional or unconditional admission by 1 June 2027
alerts: Only 21 waivers exist for 2027-2028, split unevenly across five Schools - check your School's share
No February intake waivers: the award covers the September 2027 intake only
Late webform submissions are not rescued by a timely programme application - both deadlines bind separately
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to the Master's programme, complete the waiver webform by the same date, and await the lottery outcome by 1 June 2027.

official.status_note: Open for the 2027-2028 academic year; outcomes confirmed by the end of March 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship is a cash award, not a fee waiver: TU/e states it does not cover the total cost of studies and recipients must contribute significantly to tuition and living expenses.
benefits: EUR 7,500 per academic year for two years (if enrolled and meeting study progress requirements)
Paid in monthly instalments to a Dutch or SEPA bank account
For non-EEA students part of the first-year award is funded through the national NL Scholarship
eligibility: Applied for a full-time Master's programme (or eligible track) at TU/e for 2027-2028, starting 1 September 2027
Eligible departments: Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mathematics & Computer Science
Completed a non-Dutch high school diploma or bachelor's degree
Not completed higher education in the Netherlands (exchange allowed)
Excellent academic results, GPA at least 7.5/10
Not applying for a joint Master's with Tilburg (JADS) or a European Double Degree programme
requirements: Submit the complete Master's application by 1 January 2027, 23:59 CET
Confirm in the application that you wish to be considered for the scholarship
Include a brief motivation explaining why you are a strong candidate
Obtain a Dutch entry visa and residence permit (non-EEA students)
documents: Complete Master's application including the scholarship checkbox
Brief motivation text inside the application
Latest grade transcript demonstrating GPA of at least 7.5/10
selection_criteria: Eligibility screen by the TU/e International Office, then ranking by the Scholarship Selection Committee
Only about 2% of applicants receive the award
Selection outcome cannot be appealed and the amount is non-negotiable
coverage: Cash award of EUR 7,500 per academic year; tuition, living and travel costs are not covered
application_method: Apply for the Master's programme and opt in for scholarship consideration within the same application
official.application_route: Automatic consideration through the Master's application; no separate scholarship form
official.international_eligibility: Open to international students: about 35 awards, 20 for EEA and 15 for non-EEA students
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Master's programmes in Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or Mathematics & Computer Science (listed tracks)
official.duration: Two years, conditional on study progress
official.description: TU/e awards approximately 35 Scholarship for Excellence places to international students applying to selected Master's programmes in microchip-related departments, funded by the national Beethoven Program.

not_confirmed: english_requirement (not stated on the scholarship page; programme admission requirements apply)
verification.notes: All figures read live from TU/e's own scholarship page for the 2027-2028 academic year.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a cash award on top of your own funding, not a fee waiver: budget roughly EUR 7,500 per year against a Dutch Master's whose tuition and living costs run far higher, and treat the two-year duration as conditional on hitting 45 ECTS in year one. With only about 2% of applicants funded, the motivation text inside the application is the only part you actually control - make it specific to microchip innovation.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong non-Dutch-educated applicants (GPA 7.5+/10) to TU/e's Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or Mathematics & Computer Science Master's programmes who can self-fund most costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your target programme sits in one of the four eligible departments (or a listed track)
Check your transcript converts to at least 7.5/10 on the Dutch scale
Prepare the application early for the 1 January 2027, 23:59 CET deadline
Tick the scholarship box and write a microchip-focused motivation inside the application
Prepare funds for tuition and living costs, and for non-EEA students the IND financial proof
common_rejection_risks: A GPA below 7.5/10 on the Dutch conversion scale
Applying to an eligible department but an ineligible track outside the published list
Prior Dutch higher education, which disqualifies the award
Applying for a JADS joint Master's or a European Double Degree, both excluded
Leaving the scholarship checkbox or motivation blank in the application
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, living costs and travel are all uncovered; non-EEA students must additionally show sufficient financial means for the residence permit.
document_audit: No separate scholarship dossier - the decision rides on the Master's application and its motivation
The transcript is read for the GPA threshold, so make sure the conversion is clear
A scholarship agreement must be signed if selected
alerts: Only about 2% of applicants are funded, so treat this as a bonus, not a funding plan
The second-year instalment requires at least 45 ECTS and expected graduation within 36 months
Non-EEA part-funding through the NL Scholarship covers the first year only and cannot be applied for separately
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the Master's application with the scholarship opt-in and motivation by 1 January 2027; committee decisions are confirmed by end of March 2027.
